post.description:
Creates an individual account and e-mails a 6-digit verification code. The account cannot sign in until the address is verified. Signing up again with an address whose sign-up was never completed replaces it entirely. The answer is the same whether or not an account exists for this address, so that the endpoint cannot be used to find out who has an account.

Signing up accepts the terms of use in force: `acceptedTermsVersion` is the `number` of the version the person was shown (`GET /terms/current`). If another version has been published since, the request is refused (`409 TERMS_VERSION_NOT_CURRENT`): show the current version and try again. Until a first version is published, nobody can sign up (`503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Requires the `registration` feature to be open.

post.description:
Opens a session and returns its tokens. Send the access token with every request (`Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`); use the refresh token to obtain a new pair before the access token expires.

**Read `status`.** `AUTHENTICATED`: the session is open. `MFA_REQUIRED`: the account is protected by two-step verification and no session is open yet — send `mfaToken` and a code to `POST /auth/mfa/verify` within 5 minutes.

Send a stable random `deviceId` (created once per installation): a sign-in from a device the account has never used is reported to its holder by e-mail.

A wrong e-mail or a wrong password both answer `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`. After 5 failures in 15 minutes the client is blocked for 15 minutes (`RATE_LIMITED`, see `Retry-After`). `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` and `ACCOUNT_DISABLED` (suspended account) are only returned when the password is correct. A closed account no longer exists: its former address answers `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`.

post.description:
Second step of a sign-in that answered `MFA_REQUIRED`: the `mfaToken`, and either the 6-digit `code` of the authenticator app or a `recoveryCode` (single use). Opens the session.

A code is accepted once. A wrong code answers `INVALID_OR_EXPIRED_CODE`; after 5 wrong codes the token is void (`UNAUTHENTICATED`: sign in again) and the second step of the account is blocked for 15 minutes (`RATE_LIMITED`).

post.description:
**Immediate and permanent.** Requires the current password and — if two-step verification is enabled on the account (`422` otherwise) — `code` or `recoveryCode`: an open session is not enough. `confirm` must be `true`.

The account can no longer sign in: its password, two-step verification, sessions and profile are erased at once, and its e-mail address and phone number are free for a new registration. Verification cases that were never reviewed are erased with their documents; those on which a decision was taken are kept until `legalRetentionUntil`, as the law requires. What remains is erased from `erasureDueAt`. The holder is told by e-mail.

Refused (`409`) while the account holds a back-office role — and, rarely, while another request is still modifying the account: nothing has changed, try again.

get.summary: List the versions of the terms of use

post.description:
**Permanent.** A published version is never changed nor withdrawn: correcting a text means publishing the next version. It is in force at once.

`number` must be the number of the version in force plus one (`1` for the first): a request sent twice, or prepared from an outdated state, is refused (`409`) instead of creating one version too many. `requiresAcceptance` is the rule of this version: `true` — every account must accept it before continuing (see `GET /me/terms`); `false` — it is only shown as the version in force, and accounts that accepted an earlier version are not interrupted. The first version always requires acceptance, and a new registration always accepts the version in force.

The French text is mandatory and prevails; `en` is an optional translation. Texts are plain text or Markdown — the API does not interpret them — and are stored exactly as received, at most 200000 characters each, in a request of at most 1048576 bytes of valid UTF-8. The response gives the SHA-256 digest of each stored text: compare it with the digest of the file that was meant to be published. No e-mail is sent to account holders.

The mandatory `reason` is written to the audit log. Requires `terms.publish`.

The level becomes verified, and what the case establishes (names and birth, or address) replaces what the holder declared in the profile. If an approved case of the same level was in force, it is superseded at the same instant. Answers `CONFLICT` if the case was already decided, or if **another account is already verified with the same identity document**. An internal `note` is optional. Requires `kyc.review`.

You cannot review your own case. The decision is final, written to the audit log, and notified to the holder by e-mail — who never learns who decided.

info.title: MG-Exchange API
info.description:
MG-Exchange platform API.

**Conventions**
- Versioned routes: `/api/v1/...`.
- Monetary amounts are decimal **strings** (`"12.34"`), never JSON numbers.
- Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.
- Errors use `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a stable `code` and the `requestId`.
- Every route requires `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` unless stated otherwise.
- Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header for support and log correlation.
